THE WALKTHROUGH IS ONE BULLET AND THE MISSION IS ENTIRELY IN THE AFTER-SECTIONS. This is the case AUTHORING warns about: the single top-level bullet says only that you will fight three monsters across the globe in any order, and the four sibling sections -- 'Boggelmann', 'Cryptonberry Executor', 'Dalham', 'Finishing Up' -- carry every location, every spawn and both key items. Their bullets restart at [1], so every source_bullets number below except step 1's refers to the section named in that step's note.

The three monsters share group 'monsters' because bullet 1 says in any order. Each is one rung rather than three (check to spawn, kill, check again), because none of the intermediate clicks is observable and three rungs per monster would be nine the player cannot be tracked through. Two of the three spawn on a ??? that can never carry a marker; recorded anyway, since the rung is worth keeping even without the mark.

EVIDENCE, and this is the only mission in the lane that has real evidence on more than one rung. The [KI] Vessel of light comes from the SECOND check of the Storage Compartment after Boggelmann dies, which is that step and no other, and the header's Reward is 'None' so it is not a reward. It sits on the Boggelmann rung -- the first group member, matching the page's own section order -- and NOT on a later one: it proves Boggelmann is dead and nothing else, and putting it on the last member would claim it proved all three. The consequence is that a player who kills Boggelmann first advances the mark within the group while two members are still undone; the group draws them all at once regardless, so the marker set is unchanged and only the //qm why line reads odd. That is the least-wrong of the available placements.

The [KI] Letters from Ulmia and Prishe come from Cid in 'Finishing Up' and are that rung's evidence. Two different key items on two different rungs, no duplication.

The kiting and 2-hour advice under each monster is tactics. Note that the Cryptonberry rung is really four mobs -- the NIN Executor plus three Assassins that pop shortly after -- and the page is emphatic that the Executor dies first, before Mijin Gakure. Repeatable is explicitly 'No', so false.

DIFFERS FROM chronicle_snpc, which is empty for this row: the header gives 'Grand Palace of Hu'Xzoi - Particle Gate - (H-8)' and bullet 1 repeats it, so start.npc is the Particle Gate. The mission gains a giver marker where it had none. The page is explicit about WHICH gate: the eastern one at (H-8) starts the mission, and the northern one beside the Home Point goes to the Garden of Ru'Hmet and is the wrong door. That warning is on the step.

THE ROUTE IS IN AN AFTER-SECTION. The walkthrough proper (bullets 2-5) explains the escort mechanic in prose and gives no locations at all; every grid in this ladder comes from the 'Complete Route' section, whose bullets restart at [1]. Each escort rung's source_bullets refers to that section, and each note says so.

GRID CONFLICT, and it is structural rather than a page error: the Grand Palace has an upper level (Map 1) and a basement (Map 2) that share one grid space, so (H-8) is both this mission's starting Particle Gate on Map 1 and the Ix'ghrah room on Map 2. The schema has no floor field, so the level lives in each note and the marker cannot distinguish them. That is the main reason this record is medium rather than high.

The three transporters in the route -- Map 1 (L-7), Map 2 (G-12), Map 1 (G-4) -- are movement between escorts and are not rungs. The four escorts ARE rungs and are ORDERED, not a group: each one opens the Particle Gates that let you reach the next, so the sequence is forced. Each is the same cycle -- check a Cermet Alcove to spawn a Quasilumin, keep it alive along its fixed route while it opens gates, then check it again at the alcove it stops at -- with a time limit the page states per escort and which is recorded in the note.

The aside that ten stationary Quasilumins can be talked to for a map of the area is a convenience, not a step. Bullet 5's threat list (Ix'ghrah, Eo'ghrah, Eo'zdei waiting at the end of the first and second escorts) is tactics.

No evidence: Reward is empty and nothing is handed over on this page. Repeatable is explicitly 'No', so false. The final rung leaves through the Gate of the Gods into The Garden of Ru'Hmet, which is where 8-3 picks up.
